articleBody:
Taking down old kitchen cabinets requires far more care than swinging a hammer, especially if you want to protect your flooring, save the boxes for donation, or keep existing drywall intact. 

- [ ] Clear all cabinet interiors and surrounding countertops — Prevents personal items from being damaged during work.
- [ ] Shut off water supply valves under the sink — Eliminates the risk of flooding when disconnecting plumbing supply lines.
- [ ] Turn off dedicated electrical breakers at the main panel — Protects you from live circuits running to disposals, under-cabinet lighting, or outlets.
- [ ] Verify whether your home was built prior to 1978 — Confirms if paint testing or lead-safe renovation procedures are required before disturbing walls.
- [ ] Unscrew and remove all cabinet doors and pull-out drawers — Lightens individual boxes and provides clear access to interior mounting screws.
- [ ] Cut caulk lines along wall seams and backsplashes using a utility knife — Prevents tearing off large sheets of drywall paper when pulling units free.
- [ ] Disconnect countertop hold-down fasteners and brace heavy stone tops — Avoids sudden drops that can crush lower cabinetry or crack expensive stone.
- [ ] Locate and back out hidden screws along interior face frames and hanging rails — Keeps wall studs from tearing when dismounting upper boxes.

How to use this checklist
Work through these steps methodically before pulling any cabinet away from a wall. Rushing into tear-out without shutting off utilities or locating fasteners often causes extensive wall and pipe damage.
